title: Impossible that the foreknown fail to happen in the composite sense, not in the divided sense: Judas
source_text: XXIV. Ad id vero quod objicitur, fieri non posse quin eveniant ea quae Deus ab aeterno praescit esse futura, ac proinde omnia necessario evenire, quandoquidem omnia futura Deus praevidet, ex communi Scholarum sententia dicendum est, impossibile quidem esse ut non eveniant ea quae Deus futura praenovit, sed in sensu composito solum, non autem in sensu diviso. Quibus verbis innuitur non posse simul consistere, ut aliquid sit praevisum a Deo tanquam futurum, & tamen non eveniat; Sed nihilominus, simpliciter, & absolute loquendo, rem illam quae praevisa est posse non evenire, si consideretur ex sua natura, & citra respectum ad Dei praevisionem. Exempli gratia Judas quem Deus praeviderat Christum esse proditurum, poterat tamen, siquidem voluisset, Christum non prodere. Nec Dei praescientia necessitatem illi imposuit prodendi Christum. Neq; inde sequitur potuisse falli praescientiam Dei; quia si Judas Christum non prodidisset, proditio ejus praevisa non fuisset; sed praevidisset Deus Christum a Juda non fuisse prodendum.
pass_a_gloss: XXIV. But to that which is objected, that it cannot be but that those things come to pass which God foreknows from eternity to be future, and therefore all things come to pass necessarily, since God foresees all future things, it must be said from the common opinion of the Schools, that it is impossible indeed that those things should not come to pass which God foreknew as future, but in the composite sense only, not however in the divided sense. By which words it is intimated that it cannot stand together, that something be foreseen by God as future, and yet not come to pass; But nevertheless, simply, and absolutely speaking, that thing which has been foreseen can not come to pass, if it be considered from its own nature, and apart from respect to the foresight of God. For example Judas whom God had foreseen would betray Christ, could nevertheless, if he had willed, not betray Christ. Nor did the foreknowledge of God impose on him the necessity of betraying Christ. Nor does it follow thence that the foreknowledge of God could have been deceived; because if Judas had not betrayed Christ, his betrayal would not have been foreseen; but God would have foreseen that Christ was not to be betrayed by Judas.
pass_b_english: The objection runs: what God foreknows from eternity as future cannot fail to happen; God foresees all future things; so everything happens necessarily. The common teaching of the schools replies that it is indeed impossible for what God foreknew as future not to happen, but only in the composite sense, not in the divided sense.

This means that two things cannot hold together: that something is foreseen by God as future, and that it does not happen. Yet, speaking simply and absolutely, the thing foreseen is able not to happen, if it is considered in its own nature and without reference to God's foresight.

Take Judas. God had foreseen that he would betray Christ, yet he could have refrained from betraying him had he wished. God's foreknowledge did not lay on him any necessity of betraying Christ. Nor does it follow that God's foreknowledge could have been mistaken. Had Judas not betrayed Christ, his betrayal would not have been foreseen; God would instead have foreseen that Judas was not going to betray Christ.
